$schema_note: Pre-validated swimlane configurations. Each preset specifies lane widths that sum exactly to the stated boundingBox stacking-axis dimension (h for horizontal lanes, w for vertical lanes). Pick the preset closest to your map's needs and adjust widths as needed; run helpers/lane_math.py::validate to confirm any modifications still sum correctly.
$layout_rule: For horizontal swimlanes (vertical: false), lanes stack TOP-TO-BOTTOM and each lane's 'width' is its vertical height. For vertical swimlanes (vertical: true), lanes stack LEFT-TO-RIGHT and 'width' is horizontal width. The titleBar height is INCLUDED in the lane width sum.

$shape_size_minimums.decision: 280w x 140h. Smaller diamonds force Lucid to rotate text vertically.

horizontal_2_lane_system_handoff.purpose: Two-system handoff diagram (e.g., one platform receives webhook, writes to second platform).
horizontal_2_lane_system_handoff.notes: Wider lanes leave room for 2-3 rows of nodes per lane. Reduce 'width' values if your nodes are short.

horizontal_5_lane_system_end_to_end.purpose: End-to-end flow across 5 systems (e.g., prospect-facing surface + assignment system + 3 backend platforms).
horizontal_5_lane_system_end_to_end.notes: Use the 200-tall lane for a thin orchestration system (e.g., feature flag, queue) that only needs 1-2 nodes. Widen if more.

horizontal_7_lane_functional_routing.purpose: Routing-heavy workflow inside a single system, decomposed by function (Entry, Match, Enrich, Decide, Route, Cadence, Write).
horizontal_7_lane_functional_routing.notes: The Decide lane is intentionally tall because routing maps tend to have many sequential decisions. Use horizontal canvas width (5000) for the decision row, not lane height.

horizontal_5_lane_functional_compact.purpose: Routing workflow with fewer functional stages (Entry, Decide, Route, Notify, Write). Use when you don't need separate Match and Enrich lanes.

horizontal_6_lane_functional_contact_rou.purpose: Contact-triggered routing with Entry, Match, Decide, Route/Assign, Notify, Write.

vertical_3_lane_dfd.purpose: Data flow diagram with vertical lanes (Source, Transform, Destination). Use vertical: true when time flows top-to-bottom.
vertical_3_lane_dfd.notes: For vertical: true, the titleBar runs DOWN the leading edge. Each lane's 'width' is its horizontal width. Time/sequence flows TOP-TO-BOTTOM on the Y axis.

$how_to_modify_a_preset: If a preset doesn't fit your needs, copy it and adjust. Two rules: (1) sum of lane 'width' values MUST equal boundingBox.h (horizontal lanes) or boundingBox.w (vertical lanes), INCLUDING the titleBar. (2) Recompute lane y_interior values sequentially: first lane interior starts at y=titleBar_height; each subsequent lane starts where the previous ended. Use helpers/lane_math.py to validate.
$assistedLayout_default: For maps with 30+ nodes, set assistedLayout: false on the swimLanes container so your explicit coordinates are honored. For maps with <30 nodes, assistedLayout: true is usually fine.
